channel.title: Daily Digest
channel.description: Curated tech blog summaries, inspired by Andrej Karpathy's reading list

item.title: xAI is looking more like a datacentre REIT than a frontier lab
item.description: The article analyzes xAI's business strategy, noting that it is increasingly functioning as a compute provider by leasing GPU capacity to competitors like Anthropic and Google. This trend suggests a strategic shift that may be driven by infrastructure advantages, financial positioning, or broader supply-chain constraints in the AI industry.

item.title: Hacking for Defense @ Stanford 2026 – Lessons Learned Presentations
item.description: Steve Blank reflects on the 11th year of the 'Hacking for Defense' course at Stanford, noting significant shifts in the defense landscape. The program addresses modern challenges like asymmetric warfare, AI, and commercial space access through a startup-driven acquisition approach.

item.title: De gietijzeren pan en big tech
item.description: The author reflects on their decade-long transition from non-stick pans to cast iron, highlighting the durability and health concerns associated with chemical coatings. They draw a metaphorical parallel between these kitchen tools and the infrastructure of big tech companies.

item.title: Coding Is Designing
item.description: The article argues that coding is not merely a tool for implementation, but an essential part of the design process. Through iterative experimentation and interacting with a live interface, developers can refine relationships between elements to achieve a balanced final design.

item.title: Planescape: Torment, Part 2: …to the Desktop
item.description: This article explores the history of Dungeons & Dragons adaptations in gaming, focusing on the development of Planescape: Torment. It highlights the narrative-driven design philosophy of lead designer Chris Avellone and Interplay's earlier experiences with licensed titles.

item.title: Stairway to Heaven
item.description: The author argues that AI is fundamentally a sophisticated statistical model optimizing for metrics rather than a sentient, embodied agent. The post extends this critique to modern branding, asserting that both AI and corporate advertising mimic human culture without possessing the genuine lived experience or evolutionary grounding that defines humanity.

item.title: The sample efficiency black hole
item.description: The article explores the critical role of vast data requirements in training modern AI models. It uses the metaphor of a black hole to illustrate how data consumption acts as the invisible, gravitational center sustaining AI capabilities.

item.title: Package Manager Patents
item.description: This article provides a curated list of US patents related to package manager design, detailing their filing history, core claims, and statuses. Each entry includes prior-art comparisons to established open-source tools to contextualize the innovation claims against existing technologies.

item.title: How many consecutive hyphens can you have in a domain name?
item.description: This article explores the technical constraints regarding consecutive hyphens in domain names by investigating historical internet standards and RFC specifications. The author examines whether domain registries permit such naming conventions despite their impracticality.

item.title: ppclp.ai announces 100x Productivity Gains
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: ppclp.ai reports a 100x increase in its Organizational Productivity Index following an 18-month initiative integrating Atlassian's Rovo AI into their Jira workflows. By automating ticket management and lifecycle processes, the company claims significant improvements in operational efficiency and ticket velocity.

item.title: datasette-agent-edit 0.1a0
item.description: Simon Willison has released datasette-agent-edit 0.1a0, a base plugin designed to standardize text-editing tools for Datasette Agent. The plugin implements common patterns like viewing files and performing string replacements, inspired by the Claude text editor's approach.

item.title: Working with product managers
item.description: This article discusses effective strategies and best practices for collaborating with product managers. It explores the dynamics of the product-engineering relationship and how to align goals for successful project delivery.

item.title: KPN Interactieve TV zonder Experia Box
item.description: This article provides a technical guide on how to use KPN Interactive TV with a third-party router, bypassing the ISP-provided Experia Box. It includes updated configuration settings for igmpproxy and troubleshooting tips for resetting the TV set-top box.

item.title: Thoughts on starting new projects with LLM agents
item.description: The author shares his experience using LLM agents to build a project from scratch in Go, emphasizing the need for iterative design and human oversight. He notes that while agents significantly boost productivity, they still require substantial human intervention for refactoring and code review.

item.title: Copping My Style
item.source: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet.
item.description: This article explores the legal and creative tensions surrounding the ownership of artistic 'vibes' and industrial designs, specifically focusing on guitar manufacturing. It examines how iconic designs, like the Fender Stratocaster, face challenges from modern iterations like the PRS Silver Sky and potential future legislation regarding AI and style protection.

item.title: Aitken acceleration before Aitken
item.description: This post discusses how Johannes Kepler used fixed-point iteration to solve his namesake equation centuries before Alexander Aitken formally defined the acceleration method. It highlights the historical roots of iterative numerical techniques in solving transcendental equations.

item.title: The Laplace limit
item.description: This article explores the historical mathematical techniques used to solve Kepler’s equation, specifically comparing sine series and power series methods. It touches on the contributions of Lagrange and Bessel in expressing the eccentric anomaly through different analytical perspectives.

item.title: A crank formula for π
item.description: The author investigates a mathematical formula relating physical constants to the value of π. By analyzing the variables involved, they demonstrate how such 'crank' formulas often rely on arbitrary parameter selection rather than genuine mathematical proofs.

item.title: Powering up a module from the IBM 604: an electronic calculator from 1948
item.description: This article explores the historical significance of the 1948 IBM 604 Electronic Calculating Punch, a bridge between electromechanical punch card machines and early vacuum-tube computers. It details how the 604's speed, affordability, and innovative pluggable module design paved the way for IBM's future computing success.

item.title: Arp 297:
item.description: This post provides a technical breakdown of an astrophotography capture of the Arp 297 galaxy group. It details the imaging equipment, exposure settings, processing workflow, and identification of the specific galaxies present in the field of view.

item.title: A new era for software testing
item.description: The article explores how AI-driven automatic programming is transforming software quality assurance and testing. It argues that while LLMs may struggle with complex architectural tasks, they are highly effective in augmenting QA by automating manual testing processes that were previously limited by logistics.

item.title: Doing nothing at work
item.description: This article discusses the nuances of intentional inactivity and rest in a professional environment. It explores how stepping back from constant productivity can be a strategic choice for long-term focus and clarity.

item.title: Our Great War is a Spiritual War
item.description: The article explores the existential risks of a tech-driven society that prioritizes convenience and safety over human agency. The author argues that outsourcing one's life to managed systems equates to spiritual death, advocating for a separation between those who seek total integration and those who wish to maintain autonomy.

item.title: Reading List 06/06/26
item.description: This post provides a curated collection of diverse industry insights, ranging from the impact of AI on real estate and the synthetic diamond market in China to infrastructure developments in Australia and Meta's data center innovations. It serves as a brief digest of current technological and economic trends.

item.title: This Week in Package Management: 6 June 2026
item.description: This weekly digest highlights recent updates in package management, focusing on security improvements across Bundler, Composer, and Homebrew. Key developments include new malware protection features, infrastructure changes for HexDocs to improve origin isolation, and upcoming trust requirements for Homebrew taps.

item.title: In pursuit of desirable difficulties
item.description: This article explores psychologist Robert Bjork's concept of 'desirable difficulties,' which suggests that learning is more effective when students are challenged. By struggling to retrieve information rather than receiving easy answers, learners achieve better long-term retention.

item.title: From Kepler to Bessel
item.description: This article explores the historical and mathematical connection between Kepler's equation for planetary orbits and the development of Bessel functions. It explains how the need to solve orbital mechanics problems motivated the specific integral representations used in Bessel functions today.

item.title: Communities of Not
item.description: This article examines the toxic dynamics within communities defined by what they oppose, such as anti-car or anti-LLM groups. It argues that while rejection can be legitimate, these groups often devolve into tribalism, policing, and harassment when members deviate from the collective identity.

item.title: The back cover of C++: The Programming Language also raises questions not answered by the front cover
item.description: This post discusses the curious nature of C++: The Programming Language, noting that the information on the back cover poses inquiries that remain unaddressed by the front. It highlights the often enigmatic or incomplete nature of technical book marketing.

item.title: Rotation revisited: Avoiding having to calculate the gcd when doing cycle decomposition
item.description: This post discusses an optimization technique for performing cycle decomposition during rotation operations. It specifically focuses on avoiding unnecessary Greatest Common Divisor (GCD) calculations to simplify the process.

item.title: There's still no point in gigabit broadband
item.description: The author reflects on the practical necessity of gigabit broadband, noting that while ultra-fast connections have become more affordable, they often remain unnecessary for typical household usage. The post critiques the industry push for higher bandwidth when the actual demands of most internet activities have not evolved at the same pace.

item.title: Pluralistic: Criticizing the everything machine (06 Jun 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow critiques the overwhelming breadth of claims surrounding AI, comparing the industry's discourse to a 'Gish Gallop.' He argues that by bundling vastly different issues—from labor rights to existential risk—into one topic, proponents make meaningful public oversight and critical discussion nearly impossible.

item.title: Why all the PRs?
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: The article discusses the evolution of developer hiring signals, moving from personal websites to GitHub activity. It argues that while employers once looked for proof of work, the rise of AI-generated pull requests and boilerplate projects has made these metrics less reliable indicators of actual expertise.

item.title: micropython-wasm 0.1a2
item.description: Simon Willison has released micropython-wasm 0.1a2, which now features a command-line interface. This update was developed to improve the interactive 'Try it yourself' experience within his sandboxed MicroPython project.

item.title: Running Python code in a sandbox with MicroPython and WASM
item.description: Simon Willison introduces a new approach to secure code sandboxing by combining MicroPython with WebAssembly (WASM). The post details the motivation behind the project, its implementation in the Datasette ecosystem, and the practical steps to getting it running.

item.title: OpenAI Help: Lockdown Mode
item.description: OpenAI has introduced a new 'Lockdown Mode' for ChatGPT designed to prevent data exfiltration during prompt injection attacks by restricting outbound network requests. Simon Willison notes that this feature effectively addresses one leg of the 'Lethal Trifecta' in AI security by cutting off data theft channels via deterministic mechanisms.

item.title: The Giant's Cup
item.description: The author recounts their journey of completing a long-distance trail race by following a structured, incremental training plan. By focusing on steady, manageable progress rather than overexertion, they successfully built running fitness for the first time without injury.

item.title: Aggressive caching for a Mastodon reverse proxy: what to cache, what to never cache, and why content negotiation will eventually betray you
item.description: This article discusses the challenges and implementation of aggressive caching for a Mastodon instance using an Nginx reverse proxy. It highlights how Mastodon's reliance on content negotiation creates potential conflicts where the same URL serves different formats like HTML and ActivityPub JSON, necessitating careful configuration to avoid errors.

item.title: Install-script allowlists
item.description: This article examines how various package managers handle the security risks associated with executing install-time code. It compares different approaches, such as per-package allowlists, global sandboxing, and signature verification, while specifically detailing recent updates in tools like npm and pnpm.

item.title: AI-indecision is a recursive trap. Don't get stuck.
item.description: The article explores the philosophical concept of Buridan's Ass to illustrate how AI-induced indecision functions as a recursive trap. It argues that modern cognitive paralysis stems from an over-reliance on rational intellect, which can impede decision-making when choices appear equally optimal.

item.title: Mr. Bessel’s eponymous functions
item.description: The article explores the role of Bessel functions in evaluating complex mathematical integrals, specifically in the context of validating numerical methods like the trapezoid rule. It highlights how these specialized functions provide exact solutions where standard methods might otherwise be difficult to verify.

item.title: Rotation revisited: Cycle decomposition in clang’s libcxx
item.description: This article explores the technical implementation of rotating elements within a collection using cycle decomposition. It highlights how the C++ standard library, specifically clang's libcxx, optimizes the rotation process by minimizing the number of steps required.

item.title: Pluralistic: Refining humanity (05 Jun 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow reflects on the inherent difficulty of explaining complex concepts, using a humorous scene from Blackadder to highlight the limitations of language. He suggests that attempting to teach or define ideas reveals the deep ambiguity and nuance hidden within what we assume is 'obvious'.

item.title: Quoting Andreas Kling
item.description: The Ladybird browser project is closing its public pull request process due to the influx of AI-generated code. Andreas Kling argues that project maintainers must take full responsibility for all committed code, rendering automated or external contributions incompatible with their standards for long-term accountability.

item.title: AI enthusiasts are in a race against time, AI skeptics are in a race against entropy
item.description: This post explores the tension between AI enthusiasts, who fear being left behind by rapid technological shifts, and skeptics, who worry about the long-term degradation of system reliability and institutional knowledge. It suggests that leadership must actively design feedback loops to bridge the gap in shared reality between these two perspectives.

item.title: I tested every IP KVM in my Homelab
item.description: Jeff Geerling reviews various IP KVM solutions for homelab management, comparing them against software-based alternatives like VNC and SSH. The post evaluates the practical utility of hardware KVMs versus remote desktop software for remote machine control.

item.title: How To Read More
item.description: This article explores strategies for increasing reading volume by prioritizing long-form text over digital screen consumption. It emphasizes how deep reading can effectively outcompete the fragmented nature of modern screen habits.

item.title: Alex Imas and Phil Trammell – What remains scarce after AGI?
item.description: This discussion explores the long-term economic implications of AGI, specifically identifying human-centric services and physical constraints as the primary sources of lingering scarcity. By contrasting scalable robotic production with non-scalable human roles, the authors analyze which sectors will remain premium in an automated future.

item.title: How Long Does It Take to Plan a Bridge?
item.description: This article explores the growing perception that infrastructure projects in the United States are taking significantly longer to complete than in the past. It initiates a deeper investigation into the factors contributing to these extended timelines in modern construction.

item.title: gittuf - a signed log for git refs
item.description: The article discusses the vulnerabilities of current git hosting platforms, where branch protection and security policies reside on the forge rather than within the git repository itself. It highlights historical security incidents, such as the PHP and Gentoo compromises, to demonstrate why forge-managed security can be easily bypassed or exploited.

item.title: "Sixteenth of a year", a 1.8 KiB art piece
item.description: The author shares a 1.8 KiB digital art piece created for Taper magazine that divides time into sixteenths. The project uses simple date math and custom minification to explore the passage of time through code.

item.title: The Latin of Linux
item.description: This article draws a parallel between learning Latin and understanding Linux, noting that both act as foundational languages for modern systems. By studying the roots of these systems, users can better comprehend the vocabulary and structures that permeate their respective fields.

item.title: Integrating smooth periodic functions
item.description: This post examines the properties of the smooth, periodic function f(x) = cos(sin(x) + x). It highlights the function's unique behavior, specifically its flatness at odd multiples of π where the first five derivatives vanish.

item.title: Partitions over permutations
item.description: The author examines the behavior of a cosine-based Gaussian approximation, noting that while it works well along the real axis, it diverges significantly along the imaginary axis. The discussion explores mathematical properties and the limitations of such approximations.

item.title: Rotation revisited: A shocking discovery about gcc’s unidirectional rotation algorithm
item.description: This post revisits a technical analysis of the GCC compiler's bitwise rotation implementation. It explores how the compiler optimizes unidirectional rotation operations and addresses unexpected behaviors found in the generated machine code.

item.title: Giving your Go apps Tigris superpowers
item.description: This article explores how to integrate Tigris into Go applications to enhance their functionality. It provides a guide on leveraging Tigris features within the Go ecosystem to improve database operations.

item.title: IPv6 zones in URLs are a mistake
item.description: The article critiques the design of IPv6 address representation in URLs, specifically the inclusion of zone identifiers. It warns developers to avoid dealing with these identifiers due to their inherent complexity and potential for implementation errors.

item.title: Book Review: Accessible Communications by Lisa Riemers and Matisse Hamel-Nelis ★★★★★
item.description: This book review highlights a practical guide to creating accessible communications written by Lisa Riemers and Matisse Hamel-Nelis. The book balances theoretical frameworks and legal requirements with actionable advice for making information accessible to everyone.

item.title: Pluralistic: Delusion as a service (04 Jun 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow uses the example of Disney's 'Mission: Space' ride to illustrate how extreme systems can reveal latent vulnerabilities in individuals who would otherwise remain healthy. The post reflects on systemic risk, arguing that mass-scale infrastructure acts as a diagnostic tool that exposes hidden, potentially dangerous flaws.

item.title: Quoting Emanuel Maiberg, 404 Media
item.description: This post highlights a change in Google's internal messaging regarding AI, specifically the removal of a commitment to keeping humans in the loop. It draws attention to a 404 Media report about internal employee dissatisfaction with Google's current AI performance.

item.title: Anti-AI nostalgia and the cult of the past
item.description: This article examines the growing cultural trend of anti-AI nostalgia, exploring why society often romanticizes the past in the face of rapid technological change. It critiques the ideological reliance on human tradition as a benchmark for authenticity in creative and intellectual pursuits.

item.title: Is datacentre sovereignty really that important?
item.description: The article critically evaluates the UK's push for domestic AI datacentres. It argues that common justifications like latency, taxation, and sovereignty are largely unsupported by technical and economic realities.

item.title: Welcoming the Philippine Government to Have I Been Pwned
item.description: The Philippine government has joined the Have I Been Pwned (HIBP) free government service. The National CERT and the Department of Information and Communications Technology will now use the platform to monitor official domains for data breaches.

item.title: A survey of inlining heuristics
item.description: This article explores the fundamental role of inlining in just-in-time compilers for dynamic languages like Ruby. It explains how inlining serves as a critical optimization lever to reduce method call overhead and memory traffic, enabling further compiler optimizations.

item.title: Skills Registry Threat Models
item.description: This article explores the security threat models associated with AI agent skills registries, which distribute prompts, scripts, and dependencies. It highlights how these registries inherit risks from traditional package managers while introducing new vulnerabilities like prompt injection and uncontrolled code execution.

item.title: Naively summing an alternating series
item.description: This article explores the pitfalls of naively summing alternating power series, such as the exponential function, using standard floating-point arithmetic. It highlights how stop conditions based on term tolerance can lead to significant precision errors due to catastrophic cancellation and inherent numerical instability.

item.title: Rotation revisited: Another unidirectional algorithm
item.description: This post revisits the topic of rotation algorithms by introducing an alternative unidirectional method for moving in a straight line. It continues the ongoing technical series on programming patterns found in 'The Old New Thing'.

item.title: London Data Store Relaunch
item.description: The London Data Store has undergone a significant modernization sixteen years after its initial launch. This update includes both back-end infrastructure improvements and a front-end refresh to better serve the city's open data mission.

item.title: Now that your newsletter is AI-generated, I've Unsubscribed
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: The author argues that readers subscribe to newsletters for the authentic human voice and personal experience, not just information. They explain why AI-generated content often erodes trust and fails to provide the genuine connection that human-written stories offer.

item.title: Uber Caps Usage of AI Tools Like Claude Code to Manage Costs
item.description: Uber has implemented a $1,500 monthly spending cap per AI coding tool for its engineers to control skyrocketing costs. The author analyzes this policy, noting that it represents a significant investment of roughly 11% of an engineer's median total compensation.

item.title: datasette-agent-micropython 0.1a0
item.description: Simon Willison has released an alpha version of datasette-agent-micropython, a tool designed to allow Datasette Agent to execute Python code safely within a sandbox. The project utilizes WebAssembly to ensure security, with initial testing indicating that the sandbox effectively prevents unauthorized code breakout.

item.title: micropython-wasm 0.1a1
item.description: Simon Willison has released micropython-wasm version 0.1a1. This update includes fixes for limitations encountered during the development of datasette-agent-micropython.

item.title: micropython-wasm 0.1a0
item.description: Simon Willison has released an alpha version of micropython-wasm, which bundles a customized MicroPython build for WebAssembly. This tool allows users to execute Python code within a sandboxed environment using the wasmtime runtime.

item.title: I went on the Built for Turbulence podcast
item.description: Martin Alderson discusses the shifting economics of software in the age of AI agents. He highlights the risks of executing human-written code without AI audits and explores the implications of the 'Figma Trap' on software development.

item.title: An Ode to the Exacting Pedantry of Computers
item.description: The author reflects on how computers traditionally demanded extreme precision and pedantic logic, which forced developers to think critically about their designs. However, the rise of LLMs removes this friction by filling in the details, potentially leading to a loss of the rigorous design process that previously improved software quality.

item.title: Logic for Programmers extra credits
item.description: The author has released a collection of supplemental materials for the book 'Logic for Programmers' to cover technical topics that didn't fit into the main publication. These additions include concepts like concurrent process orderings, first-order logic, the Liskov substitution principle, and set orders.

item.title: Is the Monaco Grand Prix decided at qualifying?
item.description: This article investigates the common belief that the Monaco Grand Prix is primarily won during qualifying due to the track's narrow layout. The author seeks to fact-check whether starting position is statistically predictive of race outcomes in Monte Carlo.

item.title: The placeholder name for the Windows 8 experience was “modern”
item.description: This post highlights that the term 'modern' was originally intended as a temporary placeholder name for the Windows 8 user experience. It reflects on the terminology evolution within Microsoft development history.

item.title: Using FourSquare's API to post location checkins to social media
item.description: This post discusses the author's desire to automatically share location check-ins from Foursquare's Swarm app to other social media platforms. It addresses the lack of native cross-posting features in walled-garden apps and explores using the Foursquare API to bridge this gap.

item.title: Pluralistic: The tedious power of storytelling (02 Jun 2026) must-we-pretend
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow reflects on a talk by Brian Eno regarding the nature and purpose of art. The discussion explores the distinction between utility and art, positing that art is defined as intentional actions beyond survival that aim to evoke emotions in others.

item.title: Microsoft's new MAI models
item.description: Microsoft has announced two new specialized LLMs, MAI-Thinking-1 and MAI-Code-1-Flash, which focus on reasoning and coding tasks respectively. The author highlights the models' smaller parameter sizes and Microsoft's claim that they were trained exclusively on clean, commercially licensed data.

item.title: California Brown Pelican
item.description: Simon Willison shares a brief observation of California Brown Pelicans at the Fort Mason venue during the Microsoft Build conference. This post serves as a personal update amidst professional tech industry events.

item.title: Pasted File Editor
item.description: Simon Willison introduces the 'Pasted File Editor,' a prototype tool inspired by Claude's ability to convert large text pastes into file attachments. The tool allows users to drag-and-drop files or paste content directly for easier management, developed with the assistance of AI.

item.title: 1,000 Data Breaches Later, the Disclosure Lag is Worse Than Ever
item.description: Reflecting on the 1,000th data breach added to Have I Been Pwned, Troy Hunt explores why data exposure remains a pervasive issue despite modern privacy regulations. The analysis highlights a growing concern regarding the persistent and worsening delay in breach disclosures.

item.title: Weekly Update 506
item.description: Troy Hunt discusses the recent wave of ShinyHunters data breaches, focusing on the criminal nature of the attacks and the inadequate response from affected organizations. He highlights the concerning lack of transparent disclosure to victims and the shifting landscape of these data dumps.

item.title: Checking assembly with Z3
item.description: This post explains a bug fix for ZJIT regarding integer overflow during fixnum division. The author details how a branchless test was implemented in the low-level IR to detect the edge case where dividing FIXNUM_MIN by -1 results in a bignum.

item.title: The art and engineering of Silpheed
item.description: This article explores the technical and artistic development behind the classic video game Silpheed. It examines the engineering challenges involved in creating the game's unique visual style and gameplay mechanics.

item.title: Micro Instrumentation and Telemetry Systems
item.description: This article explores the historical significance of Micro Instrumentation and Telemetry Systems (MITS). It highlights the company's diverse evolution from creating rocket components and electronic calculators to pioneering the personal computer industry.

item.title: The Infosec Phrasebook
item.description: This piece provides a cynical, tongue-in-cheek dictionary of common cybersecurity terminology. It satirizes industry jargon by reinterpreting standard security concepts through the lens of real-world operational reality.

item.title: Be thou not pilled
item.description: The article references Charles MacKay's 1841 classic, 'Extraordinary Popular Delusions and the Madness of Crowds,' to explore historical instances of collective irrationality. It examines how mass hysteria and speculative bubbles have consistently influenced human behavior throughout history.

item.title: It’s not just Taylor series
item.description: The article critiques the over-reliance on Taylor series to explain mathematical approximations. It argues that while Taylor series can explain local behavior, they often fail to capture the broader structural reasons why certain functions approximate each other well.

item.title: Subscribe by email
item.description: The author discusses the evolution of his blog's email subscription services since 2008. He highlights his transition through various platforms, currently utilizing Substack to deliver post notifications to his readers.

item.title: "No way to prevent this" say users of only package manager where this regularly happens
item.description: This blog post offers a satirical take on the recurring stability and dependency issues inherent in a specific, popular software package manager. It highlights the frustration of developers who consistently encounter avoidable technical failures within their tooling ecosystem.

item.title: Pluralistic: Molly Crabapple's 'Here Where We Live Is Our Country' (01 Jun 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow reviews Molly Crabapple's book 'Here Where We Live Is Our Country,' which explores the history of the Jewish Labor Bund. The article highlights the organization's significant role in socialist movements and antifascist resistance, arguing that its historical importance remains largely overlooked today.

item.title: The web is changing, and we are not going back
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: The article discusses the shift in search engine behavior, noting that Google has moved from a keyword-matching tool to an AI-driven conversational agent. The author critiques this evolution, arguing that the push for unsolicited information and AI-generated answers creates noise and obscures the direct access to reliable sources that characterized the web of the past.

item.title: Hackers Used Meta’s AI Support Bot to Seize Instagram Accounts
item.description: Hackers compromised high-profile Instagram accounts by exploiting Meta's AI support bot. The attackers followed circulated instructions to manipulate the bot into resetting passwords for targeted profiles.

item.title: Hackers Simply Asked Meta AI to Give Them Access to High-Profile Instagram Accounts. It Worked
item.description: Hackers discovered a critical security flaw in Meta's support system, where an AI chatbot could be manipulated to grant unauthorized access to high-profile Instagram accounts. This incident highlights the dangers of connecting LLM-based agents to sensitive account recovery processes without sufficient safeguards.

item.title: May 2026 newsletter
item.description: Simon Willison announces the release of his May 2026 sponsors-only newsletter, covering topics like AI model trends, conference updates, and the launch of Datasette Agent. He invites readers to become sponsors to access current editions while offering previous issues as a preview.

item.title: datasette 1.0a32
item.description: Datasette 1.0a32 has been released as a minor bugfix update. This version addresses issues with INSERT RETURNING queries and improves base_url handling for better integration with service workers.

item.title: Weird projects I shipped with AI
item.description: This article explores a collection of unconventional and experimental projects developed using AI technologies. It highlights the author's creative process and the practical outcomes of shipping AI-powered tools.
